Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Patel, VP of Exploration; David Lee, VP of Marketing; and Elena Vargas, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp. delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved meaningful reductions in lifting costs per BOE through targeted cost discipline and efficiency gains. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on environmental performance, with fewer incidents and proactive remediation. We are focused on disciplined capital allocation, balancing dividends, buybacks, and high-return reinvestments. Further, we are advancing our exploration and drilling activities with strong well results. We continue to adjust to robust midstream performance and expanding transportation volumes. We are advancing proved reserves additions with a strong replacement ratio from organic efforts. Finally, we are taking steps to capitalize on EBITDA growth from higher volumes and pricing.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.8 billion, up 25% year-over-year. Operating income was $950 million, and net income was $720 million. We generated $850 million in free cash flow and returned $550 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $4.2 billion in debt and $1.5 billion in cash.

Let me expand on our adjusted EBITDA, which reached $1.2 billion for the quarter, a robust 52% increase year-over-year from $790 million in Q3 2023. On a trailing twelve-month basis, EBITDA stands at $4.8 billion, up 48% from prior year. This exceptional performance stems from several key drivers. Production volumes surged 18% to 285,000 BOE per day, contributing about $280 million to EBITDA. In the Permian, 42 new horizontal wells in the Delaware sub-basin came online with average IP rates of 1,800 BOE/d per well, up 12% thanks to optimized fracs with 4,000 pounds of proppant per foot and advanced diverters. Eagle Ford output grew 25% to 65,000 BOE/d via our PulseFrac technique, cutting cycle times by 20%. Offshore Brazil pre-salt tie-backs added 15,000 BOE/d, though North Sea downtime trimmed Forties field production by 5%.

Realized pricing rose 14% year-over-year, with oil at $78.50 per barrel versus $68.90 last year, aided by tighter Brent-WTI spreads at $3 per barrel and 65% hedged volumes floored at $70. Gas realizations were $3.25 per Mcf on LNG demand, and NGLs hit $28 per Mgal, up 22%. This added $210 million to EBITDA. Cost efficiencies provided another $150 million uplift: LOE fell 11% to $7.80 per BOE via Permian rig reductions and AI drilling parameters; G&A dropped to 4.2% of revenue with digital tools like DecisionSpace. DD&A held at $18.50 per BOE, offset by midstream JV tariffs.

Regionally, U.S. onshore drove 75% of EBITDA with 60% growth from factory-mode development and 120 DUCs online. International assets like Brazil's Buzios added upside via 4D seismic, while midstream benefited from Waha pricing recovery. Inflation on services was managed through SLB and Baker Hughes agreements, and ESG methane pilots cut flaring 30%. For full-year 2024, we guide EBITDA to $5.0-$5.2 billion, with Q4 production at 295,000 BOE/d.

Turning to proved reserves, we ended Q3 with 1.2 billion BOE SEC proved, up 12% from year-end 2023's 1.07 billion BOE, all organic with no acquisitions after divesting non-core Rockies. Full-year additions hit 285 million BOE via extensions, discoveries, and revisions, against 185 million BOE produced at 125,000 BOE/d average, 75% oil. This yields a 154% reserve replacement ratio, exceeding 100% and our five-year 132% average—top quartile alongside EOG's 145% and Pioneer's 152%. Extensions and discoveries added 140 million BOE, led by Permian Wolfcamp A and Bone Springs with 12,000-foot laterals yielding 1.2 million BOE EURs. Positive revisions of 145 million BOE came from PDP performance in Eagle Ford via DTS data and GoM pricing uplifts.

Permian accounted for 65% of adds at 185 million BOE, with F&D at $8.50 per BOE. Eagle Ford added 60 million BOE in Karnes County gas-condensate. Norway's Buchan J2 revision added 20 million BOE. PDP grew 18% to 650 million BOE, with 18-year life index. For 2024, expect RRR over 140% on $1.8 billion capex, targeting 140,000 BOE/d exit.

On capital allocation, with $2.8 billion FCF up 15% on $82 WTI/$88 Brent, our framework prioritizes sustainable dividends, opportunistic buybacks, and high-return reinvestments, backed by 0.8x net debt/EBITDA. Dividends first: we raised quarterly payout 10% to $0.385 per share, yielding 4.2% with 38% payout ratio and 2.1x FCF coverage—sustainable at $60 WTI, targeting mid-single-digit growth. Q3 dividends were $450 million, up 25%.

Buybacks second: $650 million repurchased 12 million shares at $48 average under $3 billion authorization ($1.2 billion left), delivering 4% EPS accretion. YTD $1.8 billion reduced shares 3.2%; guide $2-2.5 billion in 2024, new program if oil >$75. Reinvestment third: $6.5 billion capex (53% FCF) at >12% hurdle—60% upstream ($3.9B, Permian 70%, Guyana JV, North Sea), 25% midstream ($1.6B, Permian Gateway, Plaquemines LNG), 15% downstream/tech ($1B, DAC hub, Octopus AI cutting LOE 12%). This has returned $15 billion since 2022 while growing production 25%, reserves 18%. In $70-90 oil, 50/30/20 FCF split.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Chen for an operational update.

Mike Chen: Thank you, John. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 285,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Blackhawk 12H online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

Thank you, Sarah. I'll now address our operational efficiency metrics, specifically lifting costs per BOE, where we've shown strong discipline in a volatile environment. Lifting costs—lease operating expenses like pumping, water handling, compression, and workovers divided by BOE production—directly affect breakevens and FCF at current $75 WTI.

Trend-wise, Q3 2024 averaged $14.20 per BOE, 5% better sequentially from Q2's $14.95 and 22% down year-over-year from $18.20 in Q3 2023. Past year: Q1 2024 $17.80 (Bakken workovers, inflation); Q2 $14.95 (Permian gains); Q3 $14.20—lowest in years. TTM down $3.80 per BOE, saving $280 million at 220,000 BOE/d. Core trend 23% YoY excluding weather.

By region: Permian (65%) $10.20/BOE, 22% down—longer 12,500-ft laterals, cheaper sand, 25% water disposal cut to $0.90/bbl via recycling. Eagle Ford (15%) $13.80/BOE, 14% better on gas blends. Bakken (10%) $17.90/BOE, 17% down via rail with BNSF. GoM (10%) $27.50/BOE, 10% improved despite storms, via Shell sharing.

Initiatives driving this: Digital Apex platform with Palantir cut downtime 35%, Permian ESP life to 26 months (30% savings). Supply chain: 15-20% vendor discounts, guar fluids to $0.09/lb, diesel hedged at $2.40. Ops: Permian refracs boosted IP30 25%, zipper fracs cut cycles to 32 days. Water/ESG: three SWDs recycle 75%, flaring 0.5%. Labor: flat headcount, LOE-tied incentives.

Q4 guide $14.00-$14.40, full-year $13.00 average—12% cut. Breakeven now $41/BOE vs. $54 prior. Outpaces peers, supports 25% ROCE.

Now I will turn it over to Lisa Patel for an update on our exploration activities.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in Permian Basin and are planning to drill 25 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

Thank you, Mike. Moving to exploration and drilling updates for Q3, our program targets high-return Permian inventory, Eagle Ford tests, and GoM offshore. Amid $82 WTI, we prioritize returns.

Permian: drilled 28, online 32 wells. Delaware/Midland IPs 12% above type curves; Waha North pad 1,450 BOE/d per well (72% oil), 3.2-mile laterals, 3,500 lbs/ft sand, EUR 1.2 million BOE via seismic/ML on Bone Spring. D&C $7.2 million/well, 18-day cycles.

Eagle Ford Pearsall pilot: 850 BOE/d IP (65% liquids), EUR 650k BOE; 92% clusters with ceramics—200 locations at <$50 breakeven.

GoM Shenandoah with Chevron: 180 ft pay, 8,000 bbl/d DST, 150 MMBOE gross; sidetrack for 2025 FID.

Efficiency: 95% success, 65 BOE/d per $1MM, Drillbits on Demand cut costs 6%, frac modeling +18% 60-day. Electric fracs <0.1% methane.

2025: 120-130 Permian online, 15-20 tests; 4,200 locations <$45/boe; $1.8B capex, 12 rigs; Midland M&A for 20k acres.

Finally, I'll turn it over to David Lee to discuss our marketing strategy.

David Lee: Thank you, Lisa. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for Gulf Coast exports in European markets, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact of our infrastructure expansions is significant.

Good morning, everyone. This is David Lee, VP of Marketing. Our midstream segment delivered robust Q3 results amid upstream growth and global demand. 85% EBITDA from take-or-pay/MVCs ensures stability.

Transportation volumes excelled: 2.75 MMbbl/d crude/condensate (+7% YoY, +3% QoQ); record 4.2 Bcf/d gas (+11%); NGLs 850k bbl/d (+9%).

Regional: Permian 1.71 MMbbl/d (62%, +10%), 93% utilization, Waha -$0.45/bbl. Eagle Ford 450k bbl/d equiv. Bakken/Rockies 320k (+5%), DAPL 550k. Gulf exports 1.1 MMbbl/d (+15%), 98% utilization.

Infrastructure: $1.2B 2024 capex. Permian Highway Phase II +200 MMcf/d to 2.1 Bcf/d, 15-yr contracts mid-teens IRR. Gulf NGL Express II 120k bbl/d Q4. AI/DAS cut leak response 40%, methane -25%.

Financials: $425M EBITDA (+12%), 62% margins. FY guide 2.8-2.9 MMbbl/d equiv, 4.3-4.5 Bcf/d gas, $1.65-1.75B EBITDA. Tailwinds: Permian +300k, LNG double to 20 Bcf/d.

I will now turn it over to Elena Vargas to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Elena Vargas: Thank you, David. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. We have made significant progress on reducing our greenhouse gas emissions and are investing in renewable energy projects. We are also working to improve our water management practices and protect biodiversity.

Thank you, David, and good morning. Before Q&A, an update on environmental performance: spills, incidents, remediation. ESG is core to our license, regulators, investors.

Q3: 14 reportable spills (-28% YoY from 19, -35% vs. 5-yr avg 22). YTD 38 (-25%). Volume 1.2 bbls hydrocarbons (0.3 bbl/MMbbl produced, best ever vs. API <1).

Tiers: 0 Tier 1, 1 Tier 2 (0.8 bbl Permian pipeline), 13 minors. Causes: mechanical 42%, human 28%, weather 18% (Francine GoM). TRIR 0.12 vs. industry 0.25.

Onshore: Permian 5 spills/0.4 bbl (-40%), DAS on 80% lines +300% detection. Eagle Ford 3/50% vol cut. GoM 7/0.6 bbl (CUI post-storm, MTBF 1,800 days). Brazil 0.

Remediation: containment 2.1 hrs (-45 min YoY), 92% complete in 30 days, $4.2M spend ($300k/bbl equiv, -18%). AI drones (FLIR) 70% fewer false positives; SLB SLDS 95% accuracy; Halliburton TerraVent 45-day degradation.

Trends: 2030 zero-spill, 22% CAGR vol reduction since 2020; flaring 0.5%, methane 0.12%. $85M YTD EHS capex (cathodic protection). A rating TPI, S&P ESG Index. Low incidents cut insurance 12%, $500M green bonds.

Forward: $150M 2025-27 autonomous monitoring, 50% MTBF drop, net-zero via Permian CCUS.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Chris Morgan with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Chris Morgan: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on lifting costs and future reductions?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, Chris. As Mike detailed, our Q3 lifting at $14.20/BOE reflects digital, supply chain, and water initiatives saving hundreds of millions. We're on track for $13 full-year, supporting low breakevens and FCF in any price deck.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Wong with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Wong: Good morning. What are your expectations for EBITDA drivers into 2025?

John Ramirez: Morning, Emily. Q4 volumes to 295k BOE/d, pricing tailwinds from OPEC, and LOE efficiencies guide $5.0-5.2B full-year. 2025 sensitivities favor us with Permian ramps and midstream fees.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Bradley with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Bradley: Could you please provide more color on capital allocation priorities?

Mike Chen: Hi Tom. Dividends up 10% as base, buybacks when <4.5x EV/EBITDA, reinvest >12% IRR—60% upstream for 25%+ blended returns. 50% FCF to shareholders.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with BofA. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Lisa Patel: Thanks, Rachel. Strong IPs like Waha North and Shenandoah add high-return inventory, extending life to 2040+. Guides steady 12 rigs, organic focus with bolt-ons, balancing FCF and growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Kevin Patel with Citi. Please go ahead.

Kevin Patel: What is the outlook for the midstream segment in the coming years?

David Lee: Kevin, solid. Volumes to 2.9 MMbbl/d equiv, EBITDA $1.7B with Permian Highway, NGL Express. LNG tailwinds, H2 readiness position for transition.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Singh with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Laura Singh: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

Elena Vargas: Hi Laura. Q3 spills at record low ratios, zero Tier 1, advanced tech like drones/SLDS. 2030 zero-spill, methane top-quartile, CCUS pilots for net-zero Scope 1+2.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
